transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

It is too early to say if you need a new battery or if the unit is dead, as this symptom often points to simpler issues first. The flashing red light on your V10 usually indicates a protection mode triggered by a blockage or a low/failed battery, rather than a total system failure. Since I cannot find a specific meaning for that code in my database, we will focus on the "won't run" symptom which is commonly caused by a clogged filter or blocked airway tripping the thermal cut-out. Please switch off and unplug the charger, then check if the charging light comes on when you dock it to confirm the battery is receiving power.

The charger light does come on when it's plugged in, and the blue lights come up on the battery display while charging. Filter was washed last month and the bin is empty, no blockages. Still flashing red when I press the trigger though.

Since the charger light and battery display are working correctly, we can rule out a charging fault for now. The most common cause for a V10 that flashes red and refuses to run despite being charged is a filter that hasn't dried fully or has become damp since it was last washed. Please check if the filters have been left to dry for at least 24 hours, as even slight dampness can trigger this protection mode. If they are completely dry, let's try resetting the machine by leaving it unplugged for an hour to allow any internal thermal cut-out to reset.

Filter was washed last month so it's definitely dry by now. I can leave it unplugged for an hour, but it's been sat there flat for 3 days already with the same flashing red. Battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly, if that matters. Is it likely just a worn-out battery after 4.5 years?

It is quite possible the battery has worn out after 4.5 years of use, especially since it won't hold enough charge to run the motor even when fully charged. The flashing red light often indicates the battery protection circuit is cutting power because the cells can no longer deliver the required voltage under load. Since you have already confirmed there are no blockages and the filters are dry, the next most likely cause is a failed battery or charger. Please try charging it for at least 3-4 hours in a different socket to rule out a faulty wall outlet, then press the trigger again to see if it runs.

I already tried the hallway socket as well as the usual one, and charged it for over 3.5 hours straight into the battery with the charger, not the dock. Charger light came on, blue lights showed while charging, but it's still just flashing red when I press the trigger. Is there anything else non-invasive to try, or is it time to talk to Dyson about a new battery?

[Heading: Likely cause: battery — flat or failed (cordless)]
It is likely time to contact Dyson about a replacement battery, as you have already ruled out blockages, filter issues, and charging faults. The flashing red light on your V10 indicates a protection mode, which often happens when the battery cells can no longer deliver sufficient power after several years of use. Since I could not find a specific meaning for that code in my database, we are relying on the common symptoms for this model to guide us. You should reach out to Dyson support or a qualified engineer to confirm if the battery needs replacing or if there is an internal fault with the main PCB.
